title: Qt: Lua Debugger: Freeze the main application while Lua is paused
description:
When a Lua breakpoint fires, the debugger drives a nested Qt event
loop while the global lua_State is mid-execution inside the C hook.
Letting the rest of the application run during that window caused
re-entrant dissection (paint-triggered scrolling re-entered
dissect_lua / heur_dissect_lua on a throwaway lua_newthread,
clobbering debugger.paused_L), backing-store paint races, native
macOS menu items bypassing event filters, live-capture packets
flowing into a suspended VM, and unsafe teardown when the main
window or plugin reload ran with the Lua C stack still live.

For the duration of the pause, handlePause() now:

 - Disables every visible top-level widget and QAction outside the
   debugger's QObject subtree, plus the central widget subtree (its
   setEnabled(true) cascade forces a clean repaint on resume).
 - Installs PauseInputFilter on QApplication to swallow user input
   outside the debugger and, critically, QEvent::UpdateRequest /
   LayoutRequest on the main window so its backing store cannot be
   re-entered. Input destined for the debugger or any window
   parented under it (including top-level QMessageBox popups) is
   forwarded by walking the QObject parent chain across window
   boundaries.
 - Routes QEvent::Close by widget identity so auxiliary top-level
   windows (I/O Graph, preferences, ...) survive macOS Dock-Quit's
   fan-out close pulse instead of self-destructing while their
   owning slots are still suspended on the stack.
 - Shows a splash-style pause overlay (LuaDebuggerPauseOverlay) on
   the main window that resizes with it.
 - Defers any Lua plugin reload until the C stack has unwound.

dissect_lua and heur_dissect_lua gain an early-return guard on
wslua_debugger_is_paused() to close the Lua-VM re-entry path.

Closing the main window while paused is a deliberate two-step
action: closeEvent() ignore()s the close, raises the debugger, and
records the request via a static LuaDebuggerDialog flag;
handlePause()'s post-loop cleanup re-issues the close via a queued
invoke once the Lua stack has unwound, restoring the normal
tryClosingCaptureFile / cf_close / quit() shutdown path. Closing
via the debugger dialog itself takes a synchronous unfreeze path
(idempotent endPauseFreeze() gated by pauseUnfrozen_) so the
"Save unsaved capture?" prompt and packet list stay responsive on
the way out.

Live capture is incompatible with pausing the VM (dumpcap's pipe
GSource keeps firing, and detach/reattach from outside the GLib
mainloop is fragile). A capture-session observer registered from
the existing UI-callback registrar force-disables the debugger
while a capture is running, locks the UI checkbox, and shows
"Disabled (live capture)" in the title; the user's enabled state
is restored on stop / fail.

Ping #21193

AI-Assisted: yes

+     * @brief True when a live capture is running and the debugger has

+     * The pause path (handlePause()) is incompatible with live capture:

+     * resume path). The least invasive policy is to simply turn the
+     * debugger off for the duration of any live capture and restore
+     * the user's prior on/off setting when capture finishes.

+     * in effect from process start, regardless of whether the dialog
+     * has been opened. Always called on the GUI thread.

+/** @file
+ *
+ * Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+ * By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+ * Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+ *

+#ifndef LUA_DEBUGGER_PAUSE_OVERLAY_H
+#define LUA_DEBUGGER_PAUSE_OVERLAY_H
+
+#include <QString>
+#include <QWidget>
+
+/**
+ * @brief Translucent overlay shown over the main window while the Lua
+ * debugger is paused.
+ *
+ * Renders a darkening vignette plus a centered card with a pause glyph,
+ * bold title and subtext — similar visual vocabulary to the
+ * startup SplashOverlay so the "wait" state feels native, with a
+ * somewhat more opaque treatment so the pause state reads clearly.
+ *
+ * The overlay is a plain child QWidget of the main window, intentionally
+ * *not* a top-level Qt::Window: a child widget has no platform-window
+ * identity of its own (no NSWindow on macOS, no X11 window on Linux),
+ * so it can never surface as an independent entry in Mission Control /
+ * Alt-Tab, never carry its own drop shadow or zoom animation, and
+ * trivially stays glued to the main window for free — exactly like
+ * SplashOverlay does on the welcome page.
+ *
+ * The paint is static (no animation): like the splash screen, the card
+ * is drawn once and stays put. While the debugger is paused the dialog
+ * also installs a QEvent::UpdateRequest filter on the main window
+ * (see PauseInputFilter in lua_debugger_dialog.cpp) to prevent
+ * re-entrant paints of the main window's backing store.
+ *
+ * The overlay tracks its parent's size itself: the constructor
+ * installs an event filter on the parent and sets the initial
+ * geometry to the parent's rect. On QEvent::Resize the overlay
+ * resizes to the new parent rect and calls repaint() synchronously
+ * — required because an update() would post a QEvent::UpdateRequest
+ * to the top-level main window, which PauseInputFilter swallows.
+ * QEvent::Resize itself is not filtered, so the WM's resize is
+ * delivered to the main window and we see it here as well.
+ */
+class LuaDebuggerPauseOverlay : public QWidget
+{
+    Q_OBJECT
+
+  public:
+    explicit LuaDebuggerPauseOverlay(QWidget *parent);
+    ~LuaDebuggerPauseOverlay() override;
+
+  protected:
+    void paintEvent(QPaintEvent *event) override;
+    bool eventFilter(QObject *obj, QEvent *event) override;
+
+  private:
+    QString title_text_;
+    QString subtext_text_;
+};
+
+#endif // LUA_DEBUGGER_PAUSE_OVERLAY_H
